objects.description: C++ class representing a 4-character OpenType-style tag with a trailing NUL. Provides construction from uint32_t and const char*, conversion operators to const char* and uint32_t, and equality comparison treating trailing spaces as equivalent to string termination. Intended for convenient manipulation and comparison of font feature/tag identifiers.

functions.name: ff::Tag::operator const char*
functions.description: Converts this ff::Tag to a C-style, null-terminated string view of its 4-character tag plus trailing '\0'. Use when interoperating with APIs expecting const char* tag identifiers.
requirements: The ff::Tag object must be valid and alive for the duration of use of the returned pointer.
The returned pointer refers to internal storage; do not free or write through it.
The resulting string is at most 4 visible characters followed by a null terminator.

functions.name: ff::Tag::operator uint32_t
functions.description: Converts this ff::Tag to a 32-bit integer, packing the four tag bytes as big-endian: (arr[0]<<24)|(arr[1]<<16)|(arr[2]<<8)|arr[3]. Useful for binary formats expecting OpenType-style 4CC values.
requirements: The ff::Tag object must be valid.
Result interpretation is big-endian byte order.

functions.name: ff::Tag::operator==
functions.description: Compares this ff::Tag to a C string tag. Equality is by character with a special rule: a space in the tag compares equal to a null terminator in rhs at the same position, allowing 4-char tags to match shorter null-terminated strings.
requirements: rhs must point to a null-terminated string buffer accessible for up to 5 bytes (including the terminator).
Comparison tolerates trailing spaces in the tag matching a shorter rhs terminated by '\0'.
The ff::Tag object must be valid.

functions.name: SubtableMap_new
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new SubtableMap opaque handle mapping lookup_subtable* keys to lists of kern pairs and PST entries.
requirements: Returns a non-null pointer on success or unknown on failure (no error reporting specified).
Caller assumes ownership of the returned map and must delete it with SubtableMap_delete.

functions.name: SubtableMap_delete
functions.description: Destroys a SubtableMap created by SubtableMap_new and, typically, nulls out the caller's pointer via the provided pointer-to-pointer.
requirements: p_map must be non-null and must point to a SubtableMap* previously returned by SubtableMap_new.
The pointed-to map must not have been deleted already.
After deletion, the map handle must not be used again.
Ownership/lifetime of any KernPair or PST pointers stored in the map is unknown; this function does not document freeing them.

data_types.description: A string buffer of at least 4 bytes representing an OpenType-style 4-character tag. May contain any bytes; commonly ASCII letters/numbers/spaces. Functions expecting this will read the first four bytes and may require or assume a trailing NUL at position 4 when treated as a C string.
A generic null-terminated byte string (char*). May be any length including empty, and should be readable at least up to the first NUL terminator. Used here for comparisons and general string input.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs for ff::Tag constructed from FUZZ_PARAM_STR and
# for C-string comparisons in operator==. We therefore emit byte sequences that
# are likely to be interpreted as interesting 4-byte tag strings, optionally
# followed by a NUL terminator and/or additional data, but always valid as a
# string buffer.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a short byte string that, when used as FUZZ_PARAM_STR, covers:
#   - Exactly 0..3 bytes (fuzzer stub pads with spaces to 4): triggers space/NUL
#     comparison logic.
#   - Exactly 4 bytes (no NUL): tests Tag(const char*) reading 4 bytes.
#   - 4 bytes plus NUL: ideal C-string.
#   - 4 bytes plus additional non-NUL garbage: tests rhs longer than 4.
#   - Mixed ASCII, spaces, and non-ASCII bytes.
# - Keep total length <= 4096.
# - Randomize within seeded RNG.
#
# We pack two concatenated strings separated by a delimiter pattern, so that if
# the harness reads FUZZ_PARAM_STR twice from the same buffer (common pattern),
# it can slice distinct strings. Many fuzzers split by NUL; we therefore include
# a NUL delimiter between segments and sometimes an extra uncommon delimiter.

ASCII_TAGS = [
    b"kern", b"KERN", b"GPOS", b"GSUB", b"head", b"name", b"cmap", b"post",
    b"OS/2", b"maxp", b"hhea", b"hmtx", b"vhea", b"vmtx", b"glyf", b"loca",
    b"CFF ", b"SVG ", b"STAT", b"avar", b"fvar", b"gvar", b"prep", b"cvt ",
    b"\x20RQD"  # leading space to exercise space==NUL behavior
]

NON_ASCII_SETS = [
    bytes([0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00]),
    bytes([0xFF, 0x00, 0xFF, 0x00]),
    bytes([0x7F, 0x80, 0x81, 0x00]),
    bytes([0xE2, 0x98, 0x83, 0x20]),  # snowman UTF-8 start bytes fragment
]


def _rand_tag(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randrange(5)
    if choice == 0:
        # Known ASCII tag, possibly with space padding
        tag = rng.choice(ASCII_TAGS)
        # Ensure length 4 by padding or truncation
        tag = (tag + b"    ")[:4]
        return tag
    if choice == 1:
        # Random uppercase/lowercase letters and spaces
        alphabet = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz 0123456789_-."[:]
        return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(4))
    if choice == 2:
        # Big-endian uint32 packing of random 4CC-like value
        val = rng.getrandbits(32)
        return struct.pack(">I", val)
    if choice == 3:
        # Non-ASCII patterns
        return rng.choice(NON_ASCII_SETS)
    # Mixed: 3 ASCII + 1 control/space
    base = bytes(rng.choice(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ") for _ in range(3))
    tail = rng.choice([b" ", b"\x00", bytes([rng.randrange(1, 32)])])
    return (base + tail)[:4]


def _make_rhs_variants(rng: random.Random, base4: bytes) -> List[bytes]:
    variants: List[bytes] = []
    # 0..3 bytes: stub pads lhs to 4 with spaces; rhs shorter exercises space==NUL logic
    short_len = rng.randrange(0, 4)
    variants.append(base4[:short_len])
    # Exactly 4 bytes (no terminator)
    variants.append(base4)
    # 4 bytes + NUL terminator
    variants.append(base4 + b"\x00")
    # 4 bytes + extra non-NUL
    extra_len = rng.randrange(1, 8)
    variants.append(base4 + bytes(rng.randrange(1, 255) for _ in range(extra_len)))
    # A human-readable shorter tag terminated with NUL early
    cut = rng.randrange(1, 4)
    variants.append(base4[:cut] + b"\x00")
    return variants


def _join_segments(rng: random.Random, segments: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Delimit with NUL and occasionally with uncommon delimiter to give parsers options
    out = bytearray()
    for i, seg in enumerate(segments):
        out.extend(seg)
        if i != len(segments) - 1:
            # Randomly choose delimiter
            delim_choice = rng.randrange(3)
            if delim_choice == 0:
                out.append(0)  # NUL
            elif delim_choice == 1:
                out.extend(b"\x00\x00")  # double NUL
            else:
                out.extend(b"\n")  # newline as separator
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create a base 4-byte tag used for lhs Tag(const char*)
    base_tag = _rand_tag(rng)

    # Build a set of rhs strings to exercise operator== reading patterns
    rhs_variants = _make_rhs_variants(rng, base_tag)

    # Also create an independent second tag string for diversity in the second FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    other_tag = _rand_tag(rng)
    rhs_variants.append(other_tag + b"\x00")

    # Randomly pick 2-4 segments to include; first segment tends to be a tag
    segments: List[bytes] = []
    segments.append(base_tag)  # will be padded by stub if needed

    # Add a selected rhs variant next
    segments.append(rng.choice(rhs_variants))

    # Optionally add more segments to feed further FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls, if any
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        segments.append(rng.choice(rhs_variants))
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        # Add an explicit 4-byte + NUL canonical form
        segments.append(_rand_tag(rng) + b"\x00")

    data = _join_segments(rng, segments)

    # Ensure size limit
    return data[:4096]

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs for fuzzer stubs using ff::Tag comparison with C strings.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used twice in the stub: once to build a Tag from lhs_s.c_str() (requiring at least 4 bytes),
# and once as rhs_s.c_str() for the C-string comparison that may read up to 5 bytes.
# We therefore craft a buffer that, when split by the fuzzer harness into two FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumptions,
# yields interesting yet valid strings. Since we do not control the harness directly, we encode two strings
# in a single buffer separated by a NUL, which many fuzzers use as a boundary for successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce lhs strings that are at least 4 bytes long. Include cases with trailing spaces, mixed case, non-ASCII,
#   and exact 4-char tags. Also inject the special tag " RQD" known in code.
# - Produce rhs strings including: empty, shorter than 4, exact 4, longer than 4, early NULs, and variants that
#   should compare equal due to the space-vs-NUL rule.
# - Concatenate as: lhs + '\0' + rhs, optionally add a trailing extra section to explore longer buffers, but keep
#   under 4096 bytes.

_TAG_POOL = [
    b"kern", b"GPOS", b"GSUB", b"cmap", b"head", b"name",
    b"\x00\x00\x00\x00",  # all zeros (unlikely as C string, but Tag allows any chars)
    b"abcd", b"ABCD", b"aBcD", b"1234", b"!@#$",
    b" RQD",  # known constant in code
    b"time", b"\xfftag", b"tag\xff",
]

# Examples focusing on the space-vs-NUL comparison behavior
# If lhs has trailing spaces, rhs may terminate early and still be equal.
_SPACE_EQ_CASES = [
    (b"AB  ", b"AB"),   # two trailing spaces vs early NUL
    (b"A   ", b"A"),    # three trailing spaces
    (b"    ", b""),     # all spaces vs empty string
    (b"X   ", b"X\x00rest"),  # rhs has early NUL then extra bytes (ignored by C string semantics)
]

def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(rng.randrange(0, 256) for _ in range(n))

def _make_lhs(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randint(0, 8)
    if choice == 0:
        # Exact 4 from pool
        return rng.choice(_TAG_POOL)
    if choice == 1:
        # 4 printable ascii random
        return bytes(rng.choice(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789 ") for _ in range(4))
    if choice == 2:
        # 4 bytes arbitrary
        return _rand_bytes(rng, 4, 4)
    if choice == 3:
        # 4 with trailing spaces
        base = bytes(rng.choice(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ") for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)))
        pad = 4 - len(base)
        return base + b" " * pad
    if choice == 4:
        # Longer than 4: only first 4 used by Tag(const char*), but fuzzer lhs_s is fully stored; still valid
        base = rng.choice(_TAG_POOL)
        extra = bytes(rng.choice(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ") for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)))
        return base + extra
    if choice == 5:
        # Mixed ASCII and high bytes
        four = bytes([rng.randrange(0x20, 0x7F), rng.randrange(0x80, 0x100), rng.randrange(0x20, 0x7F), rng.randrange(0x00, 0x20)])
        return four
    if choice == 6:
        # Space-equality crafted
        lhs, _ = rng.choice(_SPACE_EQ_CASES)
        return lhs
    if choice == 7:
        # Lowercase tag likely compared to uppercase rhs
        return bytes(rng.choice(b"abcdgposgsubnameheadcmap") for _ in range(4))
    # choice == 8
    return b" RQD"  # constant

def _make_rhs(rng: random.Random, lhs_first4: bytes) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randint(0, 9)
    if choice == 0:
        return b""  # empty
    if choice == 1:
        # Exact match of first 4
        return lhs_first4
    if choice == 2:
        # Shorter than 4 to test space==NUL; if lhs has spaces, terminate early before them
        # Find first space index, else 1-3
        try:
            idx = lhs_first4.index(0x20)
            return lhs_first4[:idx]
        except ValueError:
            return lhs_first4[:rng.randint(1, 3)]
    if choice == 3:
        # Longer than 4
        return lhs_first4 + b"_ext"
    if choice == 4:
        # Early NUL inside
        cut = rng.randint(0, 3)
        return lhs_first4[:cut]
    if choice == 5:
        # Different last byte
        return lhs_first4[:3] + bytes([(lhs_first4[3] + 1) & 0xFF])
    if choice == 6:
        # Entirely different constant
        return rng.choice([b"kern", b"GPOS", b"GSUB", b"xxxx"])  # valid C strings
    if choice == 7:
        # Space-equality crafted pair
        _, rhs = rng.choice(_SPACE_EQ_CASES)
        return rhs
    if choice == 8:
        # Case variation
        return bytes(chr(c).swapcase().encode('latin1')[0] if 65 <= c <= 90 or 97 <= c <= 122 else c for c in lhs_first4)
    # choice == 9
    # Random printable with possible embedded NUL at end only (C string terminates at first NUL; avoid interior NULs except end)
    length = rng.randint(0, 12)
    buf = bytearray()
    for _ in range(length):
        buf.append(rng.choice(b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789 _-"))
    return bytes(buf)

def _sanitize_for_cstring(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Ensure we do not include embedded NULs except where intended. For lhs it's fine; for rhs we rely on returned bytes.
    return b

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build lhs; ensure length >= 4 because stub pads to 4 with spaces if shorter. We'll naturally meet that.
    lhs = _make_lhs(rng)
    # Ensure at least 4 bytes for the Tag constructor semantics the stub expects
    if len(lhs) < 4:
        lhs = lhs + b" " * (4 - len(lhs))

    lhs_first4 = lhs[:4]

    rhs = _make_rhs(rng, lhs_first4)

    # Compose as two C strings separated by NUL. Some fuzz harnesses feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR by scanning for NULs.
    payload = lhs + b"\x00" + rhs

    # Optionally append a third NUL-terminated segment with random tag-like data to give additional material
    # for harnesses that consume more strings; keep within 4096 bytes.
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        extra = _make_lhs(rng)
        payload += b"\x00" + extra

    # Truncate to limit size
    if len(payload) > 4096:
        payload = payload[:4096]

    return payload
